texts.preamble: Darshan Singh vs . The State on 17 July, 2023 In The Court Of Sh. Harjyot Singh Bhalla Additional Sessions Judge-04 Patiala House Courts, New Delhi In The Matter Of: Darshan Singh Vs. The State Ca No. 89/2020 Cnr No. Dlnd01-003367-2020 Darshan Singh S/o Sh. Shiv Narayan, M/s Jagdamba Sweets, Rz-290/17, Jagdamba Road, Tughlakabad Extension, New Delhi-110019 R/o A/74, Jaitpur Pahari, Badarpur, New Delhi-110044 ......Appellant Versus The State through Fso Food Safety Officer, (Govt. of Nct of Delhi), Department of Food Safety, 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan, Connaught Place, New Delhi-110001 ......Respondent Date of Institution: 28.07.2020 Date of decision : 17.07.2023 Judgment
texts.facts: 2. The brief facts of the case as per record are that accused was running an establishment in the name of M/s Jagdamba Sweets at RZ-290/17, Jagdamba Road, Tughlakabad Extension, New Darshan Singh vs . The State on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116539014/ 1 Delhi-110019. On 31.10.2013, Food Safety Officer Sh. Ranjeet Singh alongwith Field Assistant Sh. Raj Pal Singh and Field Assistant Sh. Siya Ram, as per the instructions of Sh. Shyam Lal, Designated Officer, visited the said establishment, where accused was found conducting the business of various food articles including Khoya Roll which was lying in an open steel tray bearing no label declaration. The said sample was divided into three parts and packed as per Rules. Panchanama was prepared. One sample was sent for analysis to Public Analyst. As per the report of Analyst, the sample was found to be unsafe because total dye content of the synthetic colour used exceeded the prescribed maximum limit of 100 ppm. The report also stated that the sample contained aluminum leaves which is injurious to health. The said analysis was carried out during the period 01.11.2013 to 13.11.2013 and the result was prepared on 13.11.2013. 3. As the sample failed to pass the test, prosecution was launched by Food Safety Officer by filing complaint with the court. Accused was summoned to face the trial. Darshan Singh Vs. The State 2/6 4. Notice of accusation was served upon the accused for violation of Section 26 (2) (i) of Food Safety & Standards Act read with Section 3 (1) (zz) (v) FSSA Act, punishable under Section 59 (i) of FSSA Act, 2006 in these facts and circumstances.
texts.arguments: 7. In the present case, the counsel for the convict/accused has pointed out that the Referral Food Laboratory, Mysore and Food Analyst had indicated different tests for ascertaining the presence of Silver leaf/Aluminum leaf in the sample lifted in the present case. While the Food Analyst has indicated the test as "Nitric Acid test", the RFL has indicated the method of test as "Inorganic Chemistry by Vogel". 8. Therefore, the difference in the description of the test, in the Food Analyst report and in the report of RFL, Mysore, has been used by the Ld. Counsel to contend that the test used by the RFL in the present case is not in consonance with the Food Safety and Regulation Rules, 2011; more specifically, Rule 2.4.2 Darshan Singh Vs. The State 3/6 (7) which reads as follows: The manuals of the method of analysis, as amended/adopted by the Authority from time to time including AOAC/ISO/Pearsons/Jacob/IUPAC/Food Chemicals CODEX/ BIS/Woodmen/Winton- Winton/Joslyn, shall be used for analysing the samples of food articles. However, in case the method for analysing any parameter is not available in these manuals, a validated method of analysis prescribed by Darshan Singh vs . The State on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116539014/ 2 internationally recognized/analytic/regulatory agencies, shall be adopted. 9. Ld. Counsel submits that the description of the test in the RFL, Mysore's report does not indicate that it is a test given in one of the prescribed journal/literature i.e. in AOAC, ISO, Pearsons, Jacob, IUPAC, Food Chemicals CODEX, BIS, Woodmen, Winton-Winton, Joslyn. Counsel further submits that any other method can only be adopted if no method is indicated in the aforesaid prescribed journals. Reliance is placed upon the decision in Nestle India Limited Vs. The Food Safety and Standards, 2015 SCC OnLine Bom 4713 and more specifically, on paragraph no. 92, which is quoted hereinbelow for ease of reference:
